TUTORIALS.TUTORIAL: You need to collect energy to grow your plant by placing Collectors at the right location near their energy resource.
Each type of Collector can only gather a specific type of energy resource for your plant.
Use Defenders to protect your plant from spores. Each type of Defender has different abilities. Use them wisely.
This Risk Number indicates the total potential for damage to your Plant. As more Threats awaken it will rise.

Use the Risk Map to get a good overview of the Threats you face on each level. Notice the relationship between threats and the Risk Number. Differences in their Likelihood and Severity will require different strategies to win.
You cannot attack Threats but you can reduce the likelihood of it releasing spores by not collecting bad energy near it.
This threat is not active but could awaken depending on your activity. It’s lights indicate the likelihood of it releasing Spores.

TIPS_LOSE.TIP: Buying and positioning Defenders strategically can stop Spores reaching your Plant.
To keep risk low, try not to increase the likelihood of Threats releasing Spores.
The larger the Threat, the more Spores it can release at any one time, so the greater its severity.
Continuing to collect resources can increase the likelihood of Spores being released.
To reduce the risk to your Plant you can reduce the likelihood of Spores being released.
Upgrading your Collector or Defender is cheaper than buying another.
Repairing damaged Collectors and Defenders is cheaper than buying another.

TIPS_WIN.TIP: In both Rizk and the real world, risk needs to be managed to avoid damaging consequences.
Risk can be calculated by multiplying likelihood and severity.
You can monitor and understand severity in order to minimise risk.
This game is about 'risk management' which can be applied to many areas of life including climate change.
Risk management involves identifying areas of high risk and taking steps to reduce their likelihood and/or severity.
Decision makers identify and rank risks to produce a ‘risk register’ so they can prioritise actions to minimise risk.
In both Rizk and the real world, decision makers have limited budgets which they must spend wisely.
Decision makers can reduce the risk of climate change impacts by reducing their likelihood and severity.
In both Rizk and the real world managing risk is made difficult by uncertainty and cost.
Given limited knowledge and budgets, decision makers must assess how to deal with the different risks they face.
Understanding severity and likelihood of events can help decision makers plan and prepare for the future.
The risk of climate change impacts can be reduced by cutting greenhouse gas emissions.
